note: The acquisition policy (master plan O-1), decided for the first real canary only (CPD-0013): a conservative policy for a bounded run on about five registered outlets, not a policy for scheduled crawling and not a legal statement about robots.txt. Only public, unauthenticated, ordinary HTTP(S) is requested; no access control, paywall, bot challenge, CAPTCHA or rate limit is ever worked around: a refusal is recorded and that path stops. robots.txt: an explicit Disallow denies, an explicit opt-out denies, an absent file allows, an unreachable one defers; a Crawl-delay that is an unambiguous number binds as the minimum pause for that origin, and an origin that asks for more than crawl_delay_max_seconds is not fetched at all. One process, one request at a time, at most one request per origin in min_interval_seconds_per_origin. Raw bodies are preserved for research and project access only and are never part of a distribution package. 'external_acquisition' stays 'disabled' until the canary is armed: the switch is turned in the commit that pins the pre-canary baseline, after the crawler identity (O-2) and the preservation target (O-3) are in place.
